summary: The mixed/truncated/machine Ps.-Plutarch corpus, false true-Plutarch edges, runtime citability leak, translation links, staged/bootstrap role loss and section-to-Stephanus debt are repaired and independently regression-tested. The exact twelve-section Greek and published English manifestations are clean. Closure remains blocked only by accepted scholarly/human sign-off for the conventional pseudepigraphic attribution; Perseus itself preserves the manuscript attribution to Plutarch, and the initials A. G. must not be expanded without evidence.
resolution_criteria: Obtain accepted human-scholarly sign-off for the pseudepigraphic attribution and its dating against a named edition/study; keep A. G. unresolved unless a reliable authority expands the initials; preserve all current text, citability, translation, Stephanus and bootstrap/staged regression gates.
